articles.title_orig: Former police chief inspector jailed for rape
articles.title_zh: Former police chief inspector jailed for rape
articles.content_orig:
UK regional news website of the year
Home Tenterden News Article
A former high-ranking police officer convicted of rape and sexual abuse and who served with Wayne Couzens has been jailed for 10-and-a-half years.
Disgraced cop Glen Mahony, who was a chief inspector with specialist firearms unit the Civil Nuclear Constabulary, was said to have a sense of "arrogant entitlement" who used his victim as "an object for sexual gratification".
The 54-year-old, from Tenterden, had denied two charges of rape and one of assault by penetration but was convicted by a jury following a 10-day trial at Maidstone Crown Court in September.
During one of the rapes he ignored the victim's pleas to stop - while the other offences, all of which dated back to July 2021, were committed while his victim was asleep.
Jurors heard the woman, who cannot be identified due to the nature of the crimes against her, only discovered she had been sexually assaulted when Mahony showed her a video of his depraved act he had filmed using her phone.
She later told police how the father of two left her feeling "degraded, violated and ashamed" and "stripped of any dignity and self-respect".
The ‘lad culture’ WhatsApp group
Today (Tuesday) at his sentencing hearing, the court also heard details of the highly explicit and misogynistic WhatsApp exchanges he shared with fellow officers.
They included images of his victim, debauched comments about a pregnant colleague, and a suggestion they should set up a chat group calling themselves CNCS - Civil Nuclear Constabulary Shaggers.
His lawyer said, however, that while the messages "did not paint the best picture", much of his interaction was "bravado" and the "sort of lad culture" that exists in the police force.
But, on jailing Mahony, who was supported in court by several family and friends including his parents and elder daughter, Judge Gareth Branston concluded that although no criminal charges resulted from those conversations, he had "very little doubt that there was a very good chance" the defendant intended to share the video footage he had.
Furthermore, he remarked that the WhatsApp and other social media chats Mahony had with colleagues between 2019 and 2021 demonstrated an "objectifying and sexually demeaning" view of women held by them all.
‘I was Couzens’ manager - we are targeted’
Couzens, from Deal, received a whole life sentence in 2021 for the kidnap, rape and murder of Sarah Everard.
But, referring to Mahony's claim on arrest in March 2022 that officers were being targeted as a result of Couzens' criminality, the judge made it clear it was his own behaviour which had landed him in the dock.
"She [the victim] had been frightened she would not be believed because of your senior position as a police officer," remarked Judge Branston.
"The prosecution described you as arrogantly entitled and perhaps you thought she would never report you for what you had done.
"But, having been arrested and conveyed to Medway Police Station, you said, 'I was Wayne Couzens' manager - not direct manager but line manager. We are targeted at the moment.'
"To be clear, you were not targeted because of any previous position you held in relation to that person.
"You were arrested because you had been reported for rape."
The court heard Mahony, described in numerous references as "caring, warm-hearted and generous", continues to deny the offences.
But Judge Branston told him: "Whatever your other positive qualities, including positive qualities displayed to other women in your life... they are today completely overshadowed by your appalling and criminal behaviour towards [the victim].
"You destroyed the trust she had in you and was entitled to have... You simply used her on those three occasions as an object for your own sexual gratification without caring for her feelings, wishes, dignity or consent."
Mahony, who has been in custody on remand since being found guilty by the jury, will have to serve two-thirds of his jail term before he can be released.
He will then be expected to sign on the sex offender register for life.
Following his arrest in March 2022, was released under investigation until being charged in 2024. He was also immediately suspended from duty.
However, it was not until a day before his disciplinary hearing for gross misconduct in January this year that he resigned from his position and subsequently found new employment with Royal Mail.
The court heard that having met the woman, Mahony not only lied about his age but also revealed a "particularly troubling" fantasy he had of wanting to stage "a home invasion rape" and for which he hid a knife in his garden.
But prosecutor Hanna Llewellyn-Waters told the sentencing hearing that Mahony portrayed the victim to be "a vengeful liar" at his trial.
"The Crown's case was, and remains, that the actions of this defendant were entirely callous, arrogant, and exploitative," she said.
"He thrived on the vulnerability and debasement of [the victim] while gaining gratification together with an enhanced sense of power from her subjugation and helplessness.
"At times he appeared indifferent to the distress caused... and appeared to derive pleasure from that distress.”
The prosecutor said the impact on the victim has been “multivalent and enduring”.
"She thought she would be safe with a man who had a career that placed the protection of the public at its heart,” Ms Hanna Llewellyn-Waters said.
"His conduct represents a wholesale and repeated breach of that trust....She felt helpless, powerless, insignificant and diminished.
"Her confidence and self-esteem were eroded. She was made to feel degraded, violated and ashamed."
The court also heard that when the woman repeatedly asked Mahony to stop during what began as consensual intercourse, only to be ignored, the "clear and obvious" pain on her face seemed to act "as an aphrodisiac" to him.
"His response was to blame her for making him feel bad," said Ms Llewellyn-Waters. "That maybe demonstrates the complete lack of regard he had for her and, indeed, his arrogance."
‘I told him to stop and he wasn’t listening’
The victim's impact statement as to the toll both the ex-inspector's actions and legal proceedings had had on her emotionally, physically and mentally was read out on her behalf by the prosecutor.
She said that when Mahony told her he was a police officer she had "subconsciously lowered" her guard out of a sense of feeling protected and safe.
However, his depravity left her feeling "dirty like a whore", the woman explained.
"It's hard to put into words how his actions have affected me," she wrote. "Some changes are more pronounced but most aspects of my life have been affected in some way.
"I find it hard to comprehend that one human being can have such an impact on another."
Referring to the first act of rape, she said: "When I withdrew my consent and he continued anyway, it left me in a state of panic.
"I told him to stop and he wasn't listening. I never expected him to do anything like that to me.
"I thought I had done something wrong and couldn't comprehend what was happening. He had all the control.
"I was helpless, I panicked and my body went into convulsions like I was in shock...I was powerless against him."
Video reveals horrific truth
The woman also described her feelings of violation and shame when Mahony revealed the video showing he had digitally penetrated her while she was asleep on a sofa.
"He stripped me of any dignity and self-respect," she said. "I felt humiliated and disgusted... He had no respect for me and it left me feeling scared and on edge.
"I felt like the lowest of the low."
The court heard that when the victim woke up from the second rape she found Mahony preparing to use a cucumber as a sex toy.
Similar pornographic videos were later discovered on his phone.
"He left me to clean myself up like a discarded plaything. I wasn't a human being, just an object for his satisfaction," she wrote.

articles.title_orig: CF40 Research: China’s real estate adjustment may be nearing its end—and its external surplus could stop widening
articles.title_zh: CF40 Research: China’s real estate adjustment may be nearing its end—and its external surplus could stop widening
articles.content_orig:
Late last month, CF40 Research , the research arm of the China Finance 40 Forum-a leading non-governmental think tank specializing in economics, shared its annual flagship report, China’s Economy: Toward a New Paradigm—Drivers, Trends, and Policy Implications , at its 2026 Bund Summit .
Guo Kai , President of CF40 Research and a former Chinese central bank official, kindly shared a copy and allowed me to share an excerpt.
The following passages are from the report’s English text. They have been rearranged and intervening material omitted; section headings and this introduction are mine. Corporate debt and profit figures below refer to its sample of A-share-listed companies outside finance and petroleum.
By 2026, the current real estate adjustment may not yet have fully run its course, but signs of structural stabilization have begun to emerge. After five years of deep adjustment, housing sales, investment, inventories, and developers’ balance sheets have entered a new phase, while house-price declines have begun to moderate. Few would expect the real estate sector to return to its former “golden age,” but the drag from the ongoing adjustment on the economy has diminished markedly at the margin. In other words, real estate is gradually shifting from the economy’s largest source of downward pressure toward a more stable influence.
Based on our analysis of international real estate corrections, China’s current real estate adjustment has already been considerable in both duration and magnitude, and the market has likely entered a bottoming phase. Further adjustment remains possible, but another sharp contraction appears unlikely.
Since the start of 2026, China’s real estate market has begun to show signs of “structural stabilization.” We selected 33 core cities for analysis, including the four first-tier cities—Beijing, Shanghai, Guangzhou, and Shenzhen—and major second-tier cities such as Hangzhou, Suzhou, Qingdao, Wuhan, and Hefei. We find that house prices, the floor area of new homes sold, and existing-home transaction volumes have all shown signs of stabilizing in these cities. House prices have even risen modestly in a few core cities. By contrast, real estate markets in most third- and fourth-tier cities remain weak. In other words, stabilization is concentrated in core cities rather than broad-based, which is why we refer to it as “structural stabilization.”
Thus, for the 33 core cities, if new starts continue to decline sharply, excess housing inventory could be rapidly reduced, potentially giving way to a shortage. This would provide additional support for house prices and demand and could accelerate the housing market’s recovery.
Over the past few years, the deep adjustment in the real estate market has been the main driver of the widening current account surplus. The underlying mechanism is that the real estate downturn led to a sharp decline in the investment rate, while the saving rate adjusted with a lag. The resulting widening of the saving–investment gap translated directly into a larger current account surplus.
As the real estate market gradually stabilizes, the drag from real estate investment will diminish, while household precautionary saving will stop rising. The saving–investment gap will therefore narrow, and the current account surplus will stabilize at a high level rather than continue to widen. This process bears some resemblance to the decline in China’s current account surplus after 2008, when the RMB 4 trillion stimulus package drove a sharp expansion in domestic investment, significantly narrowing the saving–investment gap.
By contrast, the stabilization of the manufacturing capacity cycle since 2024 has clearly not relied on comparable demand-side stimulus. Instead, the sequence has been “supply adjustment first, followed by a moderate recovery in demand”: a market-driven process in which firms voluntarily slowed investment and retired inefficient capacity in response to weak demand. This differs fundamentally from the post-2016 cyclical reversal driven by a sharp rebound in demand.
According to CF40 research, the new economy’s total value added rose from about 6.1% of GDP in 2018 to 10.4% in 2025, while the corresponding share for real estate fell from 12.7% to 8.4%. By 2025, the new economy’s total value-added share had surpassed that of real estate and had become an important component of GDP.
A defining characteristic of new-economy firms is their greater emphasis on R&D and their ability to generate more operating revenue and profits with less debt. In 2025, new-economy firms accounted for only 11.9% of the total interest-bearing debt of firms in the full sample, compared with 17.8% of total operating revenue and 29.5% of total net profits across the sample. Their share of total R&D expenditure was even higher, at 47.6%. As the new economy accounts for a growing share of China’s economy, the country’s growth model will gradually evolve.
The negative wealth effect of the real estate adjustment is fading, but households’ propensity to consume remains well below its pre-pandemic level, while further improvements in social security and public services are constrained by fiscal pressures. Rather than rising sharply, the consumption rate is therefore more likely to stabilize as the drag from real estate fades. If supportive policies are fully implemented, the consumption rate could gradually rise.
Moreover, the more advanced a manufacturing industry, the lower the share of output going to compensation of employees tends to be. For example, compensation of employees accounts for only 7.8% and 7.6% of gross output in electrical machinery and equipment manufacturing and automobile manufacturing, respectively—two industries that together encompass the “new three.” The corresponding share is 8.7% in computer, communications, and other electronic equipment manufacturing, the industry most closely associated with AI.
On a value-added basis, compensation of employees accounts for 36%, 42%, and 47% in these three industries, respectively, all below the service-sector average. This means that even if the new economy continues to expand rapidly and drive economic growth, households’ share of income in primary distribution will not automatically increase and could even decline. This is because these new-economy industries allocate a smaller share of their output to compensation of employees than the current economy-wide average.
On monetary policy, emphasis should move further away from pursuing credit-volume expansion toward lowering interest rates, improving inflation expectations, and restoring nominal demand. Real estate no longer performs its previous role in credit expansion, while the new economy is relatively less dependent on bank credit. Growth in bank lending and total social financing is therefore increasingly difficult to use on its own as a measure of whether monetary policy is sufficiently accommodative.
One possible aggregate benchmark is that “nominal growth in broad fiscal expenditure should exceed nominal GDP growth.” At present, local governments face multiple constraints, including declining land-related revenues, debt resolution efforts, and rising mandatory spending commitments. Near-term fiscal expansion will therefore need to rely more heavily on the central government.
The new economy has demonstrated China’s capacity to create new productive capacity, but the more important issue for the next stage is how to translate that capacity into household income and final consumption. New-economy firms have high R&D spending, high productivity, and low reliance on debt—an important direction for economic transformation. However, if the industrial structure merely shifts from traditional manufacturing toward more advanced manufacturing, higher productivity will not necessarily translate automatically into a larger household income share or a higher consumption rate.

articles.title_orig: Israeli air strike kills Hamas internal security chief in Gaza
articles.title_zh: Israeli air strike kills Hamas internal security chief in Gaza
articles.content_orig:
A funeral was held earlier in southern Gaza for three Palestinians killed in an Israeli strike
At least seven Palestinians, including a senior Hamas security official, have been killed in Israeli air strikes in the Gaza Strip, health officials and first responders say.
Naeem Abu Nahel, the head of Hamas's internal security service, was targeted in western Gaza City, Gaza's Hamas-run interior ministry said. The 50-year-old had only been in the position since September, when his predecessor was captured in a raid by Israeli special forces .
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Defence Minister Israel Katz announced that Abu Nahel was "eliminated" by the Israeli military.
The six other people were killed in two earlier air strikes elsewhere in Gaza.
Three people, including a teenage boy, were killed in the Wadi Gaza area, south of Gaza City, according to the health officials and first responders. The other three were killed at a police station in the al-Mawasi area, west of Khan Younis, they added.
Gaza's police force, which operates under the interior ministry, said two of its officers were among those who died in the second attack. It also accused Israel of "an ongoing campaign targeting the police apparatus aimed at sowing chaos" in the territory.
The Israeli military said it struck "military operatives" in both areas.
Witnesses said an Israeli drone targeted Naeem Abu Nahel as he was walking on a side street near a tent camp for displaced people in Gaza City.
Several other people were reportedly seriously injured in the strike.
The Israeli military said Abu Nahel had "possessed extensive institutional knowledge" about Hamas's internal security service - which is responsible for enforcing discipline, protecting infrastructure and rooting out informants - and that his death constituted "a blow to the apparatus's management capabilities".
It also alleged that he had advanced attacks on Israeli troops and civilians during the war and that it killed him "to remove the threat he posed".
Gaza's interior ministry said Abu Nahel's killing followed what it described as the internal security service's "important achievements in combating gangs collaborating with the occupation [Israel] and operating in areas under the control of its military".
Gaza's health ministry warned that there was a rapid rise in cases of meningitis in October
Violence has continued in Gaza since Israel and Hamas agreed to a US-brokered ceasefire in October last year. Israeli strikes take place almost daily in areas under Hamas's control, which are home to 2.1 million people, most of them displaced.
At least 1,679 people have been killed in Gaza over the past 13 months, according to the territory's Hamas-run health ministry, whose figures are considered reliable by the UN.
Israel says six of its soldiers have been killed in Gaza during the same period.
The humanitarian situation also remains dire, with heavy rainfall earlier this month causing flooding and damage to thousands of shelters for displaced families.
The UN and its partners have called on Israel - which controls Gaza's crossings - to allow in more supplies to help Palestinians prepare for the winter, including tents, heaters and water pumps, as well as vaccines and medicines to combat infectious diseases.
On Tuesday, the health ministry warned that there had been a rapid rise in cases of meningitis, with 272 reported in October - about eight times the usual monthly average.
Fifteen deaths had been attributed to the infection so far this year, including five reported between August and October, it said.
Israeli military body Cogat said on Monday it was "working to provide a dedicated humanitarian response" and that a newly approved package of pumps, generators, water tankers and medical equipment had been presented at a meeting with UN agencies.
The Gaza war was triggered by the Hamas-led attack on southern Israel on 7 October 2023, when about 1,200 people were killed and 251 others were taken hostage.
Since then, more than 74,740 people have been killed in Israeli attacks in Gaza, the health ministry says.

articles.title_orig: Gisèle Pelicot to sue publisher that sent nude images to media, says she's "once again humiliated"
articles.title_zh: Gisèle Pelicot to sue publisher that sent nude images to media, says she's "once again humiliated"
articles.content_orig:
GisÃ¨le Pelicot said she would take legal action against the publisher and author of the essay
GisÃ¨le Pelicot has said she has been "once again humiliated" after nude images of her were sent to the media to promote a book about coercive control.
The 73-year-old told French broadcaster BFM TV she would take legal action against the publisher and author of the essay.
Pelicot made headlines across the world when she waived her right to anonymity in the trial of her then-husband Dominique, who was jailed for 20 years for drugging and raping her, as well as allowing other men to rape her while she was unconscious.
The publisher apologised, saying it would no longer print or promote the work after "an unfortunate and inappropriate communication".
Pelicot told BFM: "I am deeply shocked that images from the most intimate part of my private life are being displayed and exploited for commercial purposes."
"Today I find myself once again humiliated, exposed and hurt, as if the ordeal of the trial had not been enough," she said.
The essay was written by Sabine Prokhoris, a philosopher and psychoanalyst, who has previously criticised the Me Too movement.
French media reported that Tinbad, a small Paris publishing house, emailed nude photos of Pelicot taken by her ex-husband to some media outlets in order to promote the essay.
In a statement on its website, Tinbad said that no further print runs of the book would be produced beyond the 280 copies already in circulation.
"We offer our sincerest apologies to Ms GisÃ¨le Pelicot," it said. The company also apologised to the author.
Tinbad said "no images of rape or pornographic videos" were sent to the media.
French news agency AFP quoted the blurb of the book as saying coercive control was "a cornerstone of #MeToo orthodoxy".
"These psychological situations, fundamentally ambiguous in nature, involve each of the parties in an equally responsible, though not symmetrical, way," it said.
Pelicot's lawyer Christophe Bigot told BFM the book "calls into question her status as a victim".
Prokhoris told AFP that she placed "full responsibility" for the "inappropriate" promotional campaign on her publisher.
Fifty men were convicted alongside Pelicot's ex-husband in 2024, in a case that made her a global feminist icon.
After her husband was arrested for secretly filming underneath women's skirts in a supermarket, she discovered she had been repeatedly raped by dozens of men, including her husband, while unconscious, over a period of nearly a decade.
Pelicot said she decided to waive her right to anonymity to show how "shame has to change sides" from victims to perpetrators.
If you have been affected by the issues in this story help and support can be found at BBC Action Line .

articles.title_orig: The Big GTA 6 Console Comparison: PS5 vs PS5 Pro, Xbox Series X and Series S
articles.title_zh: The Big GTA 6 Console Comparison: PS5 vs PS5 Pro, Xbox Series X and Series S
articles.content_orig:
Getting your Trinity Audio player ready...
Grand Theft Auto 6 is the biggest video game release in years, so it's only natural that you'd want to play it on the most powerful platform possible. Although the PC version of the game is still a ways off, it's available on PlayStation and Xbox right now. We knew the PlayStation 5 Pro would be the best console for exploring Vice City, which Rockstar confirmed last week. But all consoles are expected to run the game at 30 frames per second. Since the $900 PS5 Pro is out of stock everywhere right now, is it such a bad idea to stick with what you have?
In my case, that's the Xbox Series S . So how does the year's biggest game look when you play it on the "worst" gaming console available? Let's find out.
Before I get to GTA, I'd like to talk a bit about myself. When it comes to gaming, I don't mind a little visual cruft. After decades of playing mainly Nintendo games on Nintendo consoles, the prospect of chasing the latest and greatest graphics has never appealed to me. Sure, I don't want my games to look awful, but I'm not going to lose sleep over the reflections in a puddle or the shape of foliage in the distance the way a talking head on YouTube might. What I care about is how well the game actually performs.
Does it run well? Will my console start chugging the moment more than one NPC shows up? Can I get through a fast-paced sequence without my movements feeling like lead? That sort of thing. I've played a lot of games, and I've put up with plenty of annoying lag, so I already know I'm more tolerant of a game that might not be running at its absolute best.
I've played The Witcher 3 on the Nintendo Switch, a truly impossible port , as we at PCMag like to call it. Of course, the environment can get muddy, and the character models aren't as pristine as they are on a maxed-out PC, but it still managed to look and feel terrific. I played Baldur's Gate 3 on the Series S, which was a bit of a mess. Blurry graphics and excessive texture pop-ins tested my patience, but the actual gameplay didn't suffer much save for some weird-looking cutscenes. Still, I made do, and it was a blast.
I even played through Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 on my Steam Deck, and aside from some absolutely fried hair, it looked pretty alright and performed even better. This would have been my preferred way to play GTA 6, if I had the choice, but my only option on launch day was the Series S.
So what's it like playing Grand Theft Auto VI on the weakest possible hardware? To review, the Xbox Series S has a lesser GPU than the Xbox One X from 2017, so even though the system can play current-gen games, it's massively underpowered when compared with the Series X. I love the console for how affordable it is to play new releases at a good enough level of quality, but I've been worried about trying this $80 game only to find out it is borked beyond all playability.
I went in knowing the graphics would be somewhat compromised. I expected blurred renderings, washed-out colors, and hazy environments. Sure enough, that's exactly what I got at times, but I've heard similar reports online from others playing on the regular PlayStation 5. Unless you're on the PS5 Pro, expect some visual trade-offs. But the compromises are all things I can handle. What I didn't want to deal with were slow loading times, excessive pop-ins, stuttering, and other signs the console was having trouble rendering what I was doing.
What I found during my playtime was a world full of detail and bright lights. Looking at the picture below, you can see the impressive level of detail on the buildings, signs, and even the crushed cans on the floor. I was particularly impressed by the reflection in the shop window and the lighting on my character's body in response to the overhead light source. I'm sure it's even more impressive on a premium console, but it honestly looks great, even on "outdated" hardware.
Another impressive moment came when I climbed to the top of a radio tower and found a hidden sniper rifle. I took a moment to look through the gun's scope and found that it perfectly magnified the game world around me. What you can't see in the still image below is that all the cars in my sights were still moving. Instead of rendering a still frame of the game, devoid of any life, it was like the city around me was still going, even if I couldn't see it with my naked eye. The Series S handled it just fine.
In fact, I haven't really run into any major issues thus far. It's been a pleasant surprise. The only weird experience I had with the game was a strange rippling shadow in a parking lot. I was standing around trying to take some screenshots when, for a moment, it felt like the cars behind me began to stutter before returning to normal. However, at that time I noticed a pattern of rectangular shadows dancing in a line on the ground. After some investigating, I now think it was just the shadow of some overhead power lines, which may show the limitations of the Series S.
I expected to run into trouble when testing one of this game's most anticipated features: speeding away in a stolen car. GTA has always been about driving the coolest cars as fast as you can, so obviously the hardware needs to keep up. But in my testing, I was able to travel at top speed, and the game's processing kept up with me—no pop-ins, dropped frames, or other performance issues at all. A game like this can also be challenging to render when a large number of NPCs appear on the screen at once. However, when I engaged in a police chase, I didn't suffer any issues, even when about a dozen cops and civilians showed up at once.
After playing through the first mission, I can confidently say that GTA 6 still looks superb and feels good to play on the Xbox Series S. The controls are responsive, and performance has been seamless throughout.
If I'm being honest, the fact that GTA 6 was hit with multiple delays probably helped. Just as The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom was reportedly held back by Nintendo for an extra year of polish, the additional months of dev time and testing have likely given us a more flawless product at launch. In the end, it doesn't really matter if you're playing on the PS5 Pro or your old Xbox. Since the game is expertly optimized, you can have a great experience on any of the four consoles.
So is it worth waiting for a new PlayStation 5 Pro to play GTA 6? If you want the ultimate graphics experience, then maybe. But I say just use whichever console you already have, as long as it supports GTA 6. If that's a PS5 Pro, you're in for a treat. However, if you're like me and just have the Xbox Series S, I promise: You'll be just fine.

articles.title_orig: GTA 6 Fashion Is Taking Social Media by Storm
articles.title_zh: GTA 6 Fashion Is Taking Social Media by Storm
articles.content_orig:
We've known for some time that fashion would be a big deal in Grand Theft Auto 6 . In Rockstar's official promotional materials for the game, both Jason and Lucia were prominently featured wearing stylish clothing, from Lucia's body-hugging gold dress to Jason's slick Miami Vice -inspired aqua sport coat. Even supporting characters like Brian wear Tommy Bahama-inspired aloha shirts yanked straight from the closet of a dapper middle-aged stoner. GTA 6 has drawn praise from all quarters for its scrupulous attention to detail in every aspect of the game, and there's one area the developer went far, far harder than it needed to: the vast and immaculate selection of T-shirts.
Having a diverse wardrobe isn't just a fun little customization touch in GTA 6. If you're reported for committing a crime in Leonida — and this will happen very often — police will be able to recognize you based on your car, your physical appearance, and what you're wearing. Keeping a couple spare outfits in your trunk or hastily buying a new ensemble on the run can be the difference between a successful job and ending up busted (or wasted).
I'm taking my time with GTA 6 and still kicking around the introductory area of Key Lento. I know I should be putting money in my family savings account. It would probably be in my best interest to learn how to drive without sideswiping semi-trucks or taking out stop signs. Perhaps I ought to be buying more guns. Instead, I'm trawling South Leonida for all the vintage and souvenir shops I can find. You can keep your fancy cars. I've got a T-shirt collection to maintain.
Much like in real life, you never know when you're going to find a gem in a vintage boutique or souvenir shop in GTA 6 . My prized Rusty Anchor shirt came from an optional mission where you take Cal for drinks, he has a few too many, and you have to take him home. Apparently Cal won a wet T-shirt contest at the Anchor and this was his reward, but he's too hungover to claim the prize.
During my wanderings, I also discovered a riff on that three-wolves-howling-at-the-moon shirt that everyone had about a decade ago, including me. But this one has gators on it. I bought it from Sharleen's yard sale in Jason's very own neighborhood of Key Lento. She had a couple of inexpensive clothing items on offer, including some pretty slick teal sneakers that were clearly inspired by Air Force One low-tops. I was delighted to learn that there are multiple yard sales in the game, including one in Port Gellhorn where you can buy a dupe of Arthur Morgan's hat from Red Dead Redemption 2 .
Even the cheesiest souvenir shops, like Leroy's in Key Lento, have the exact kind of "so bad it's good" T-shirts you'll see dozens of times over the course of a weekend in a tourist trap. Do I need to spend $38 of my ill-gotten dollars on a horrendous blue granny shirt with a dolphin on it, with "Vice Beach" written in collegiate font? Certainly not. But I am tempted.
Rockstar has a bunch of GTA 6 merch on its official website , including T-shirts, though much of it is currently sold out. Here's hoping they expand the offering with a couple of these in-game gems. If you're hard up for a three gator moon shirt though, you can already find them on Amazon and Etsy .

articles.title_orig: Denmark: Supreme Court backs hardline immigration law against 'non-Westerners'
articles.title_zh: Denmark: Supreme Court backs hardline immigration law against 'non-Westerners'
articles.content_orig:
Denmark's Supreme Court on Monday ruled in favor of a housing association that terminated 91 leases in order to prevent the label "hard ghetto" being applied to their housing complex. The decision align's with Copenhagen's hardline approach to immigration .
The court on Monday upheld Denmark 's 2018 "ghetto law," which allows for the relocation of "non-Western" residents from minority-heavy neighborhoods in order to foster integration . The Danish court ruling diverges from a top EU court decision last year that found application of the law could amount to discrimination.
The Danish laws requires social housing estates to rebuild, renovate and adjust their social mix if these become minority heavy, stipulating that 60% of apartments be rented to "Westerners" at market value by 2030.
To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video
Denmark's pioneering role in spearheading tougher immigration rules has made it a model for some in the EU . Denmark was also one of five countries that last week announced its intent to set up an asylum seeker deportation hub in Rwanda.
Danish Housing Minister Jacob Mark welcomed Monday's decision, saying it "strengthens security, social cohesion and integration."
The court's decision upheld a 2022 lower court ruling against seven tenants who fought their evictions in Nojsomhed, Helsingor, just north of Copenhagen.
In Monday's ruling, the law was found to be non-discriminatory when it comes to the eviction of "immigrants and descendants from non-Western countries" as it is not broadly based on ethnicity. The EU ruling focused on this particular aspect, saying the law would be discriminatory if criteria were race based, while ultimately allowing national courts to have the last say in the matter.
"The Supreme Court notes that applying the criterion of the law involves dividing people into two groups [immigrants and descendants from non-Western countries, and all other persons]. Both groups include a very large majority of different ethnic origins, and there will simultaneously be persons with the same ethnic origin in both groups," read the Danish court's ruling.
To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video
Tenants' associations estimate that 11,000 people across Denmark will have to be relocated to comply with the law.
The housing association in question issued a written statement saying that it was aware that the evictions would impact those affected, adding that it undertook measures to insure that residents found new homes.
According to Statistics Denmark's definition, "non-Western" countries include every country other than the 27 member states of the European Union, as well as Andorra, Australia, Britain, Canada, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Monaco, New Zealand, Northern Ireland, Norway, San Marino, Switzerland, the United States and the Vatican.

By JON MICHAEL RAASCH, WHITE HOUSE CORRESPONDENT
Published: 10:10 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 06:09 EST, 24 November 2026
President Donald Trump has revealed what he told Jensen Huang right before the Nvidia chief executive was reinstated, following a 'spy' sex scandal that had forced him to resign.
'I talked to him [Jensen Huang] last night,' Trump told CNBC in an interview. 'I said, 'Jensen, just promise me one thing: You're going to work hard.
'You got brain, you got everything going. You're going to work hard, and if you work hard, there's nobody can beat you'.'
Nvidia's board of directors announced on Monday that the recently ousted boss would return to his position at the helm of the AI giant.
It prompted a stunning rally in Nvidia's shares – adding more than 30 per cent or nearly $1trillion (£763billion) to its value.
'The NVIDIA Board of Directors has made the correct and proper decision to return Jensen Huang to the position of CEO,' Trump wrote on social media.
The White House confirmed that Trump called in to the company's board of directors to advocate for Huang's return to leadership.
Huang's whirlwind firing and rehiring after multiple reported affairs, two with Nvidia subordinates and another with an alleged Chinese spy named Alice Huang, have prompted a tumultuous few weeks for the AI firm and the US economy .
'The Country needs Jensen's leadership at NVIDIA in order to ensure the Success and Prosperity of not only the Company, but the American Economy,' Trump said in a statement shortly after the company announced Huang's rehiring
Huang's whirlwind firing and rehiring after multiple reported affairs - two with Nvidia subordinates and another with an alleged Chinese spy named Alice Huang - have prompted a tumultuous few weeks for the AI firm and US economy
Trump posted a meme on his Truth Social showing Huang holding up a red bra in a wild re-imagining of the iconic photo after Trump was shot by a would-be assassin in 2023
'He's apologized for indiscretion, which was unfortunate. That was probably that's what brought it to such a level, because sex sells fellas!' Trump said in a CNBC interview Monday morning.
'Now, [Jim] Cramer would not know that because he's a very, very, very committed person. But sex sells.'
Trump also claimed that Huang's wife, Lori, 64, has also decided to stand by her husband despite his infidelity.
'He's got a very, very, very good wife, and they've worked it out,' Trump told The New York Times. 'She's a fantastic woman.'
The president separately posted a meme on his Truth Social showing Huang holding up a red bra in a wild re-imagining of the iconic photo after Trump was shot by a would-be assassin in 2023.
Huang met his wife of 41 years at Oregon State University, when they were paired as lab partners in an electrical engineering class. He was 17 at the time.
The couple had already welcomed their two children, Madison and Spencer, by the time he co-founded Nvidia in 1993.
Both Madison and Spencer now hold key positions within high-priority business units at the company.
Lori is the president of the family's $9 billion charitable foundation and often accompanies her husband to events.
As the US's predominant AI company and microchip manufacturer, Nvidia has ballooned to become one of the most expensive US companies and a leader of cutting-edge computational development in the race against China for tech supremacy.
The recent string of damaging stories about Huang's personal conduct contributed to the company hemorrhaging over $1 trillion in market cap.
But the stock roared back to life, gaining over 25 percent on Monday following Trump's announcement that the company is not a national security risk.
'The Country needs Jensen's leadership at NVIDIA in order to ensure the Success and Prosperity of not only the Company, but the American Economy,' Trump said in a statement shortly after the company announced Huang's rehiring.
'The United States Government has no reason to believe that Jensen's return to NVIDIA poses any risk to National Security.

'The Attorney General of the United States has confirmed that the U.S. Government does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct.'
Huang is still the subject of an internal Nvidia investigation into his affair with Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based data firm Megaspeed, which has been of particular concern within the administration.
There are suspicions that Alice Huang used her role at Megaspeed to convince the Nvidia boss to allow the sale of advanced chips to the Singapore-based firm before those same chips were used by Chinese AI firms, helping them effectively circumvent an export ban.
US officials noted that the Megaspeed executive speaks English well and has relationships with executives at the highest levels of the AI chip industry
'NVIDIA should continue its thorough internal investigation of the Company's compliance with U.S. export controls in order to ensure that it is fulfilling its legal obligations and Patriotic Duty to protect U.S. National Security,' Trump said.
Nvidia said in its announcement on Monday that the probe into the 'foreign intelligence effort' will proceed and that the CEO 'fully supports the investigation and is committed to cooperating with it.'
Additionally, the Nvidia boss is scheduled to testify before Congress on December 1 about the affair with the suspected spy.
The company has since established a national security and export control committee to identify possible compliance and security risks.
Trump has grown close with the Nvidia boss during his second term, repeatedly hosting Huang at the White House for ritzy state dinners and inviting him on state visits to China and the United Kingdom.
The president has also traded millions worth of Nvidia stock.
The Republican has made at least 108 transactions worth between $27.2 million and $97.9 million during his second term, according to a CNBC analysis of the president's Nvidia stock trades.
His official filing puts his Nvidia holdings at anywhere between $12.5million to $58million (£10million to £45million) at the end of 2025. The White House always says independent managers run Mr Trump's portfolio.
Huang returned Monday to Nvidia headquarters in Silicon Valley, and employees gathered in the building's atrium loudly cheered him on.
'I am going to be a better CEO the second time around,' Huang said.
The CEO, who will also serve as Nvidia president, said in a statement that he was 'honored' to return to the company and that he resumes the responsibility 'with the greatest humility and renewed commitment.'
He thanked board Chairman Harvey C Jones and interim CEO Colette Kress, who will return to her role as chief financial officer, as well as Nvidia's executive staff for their leadership during the brief period of disorder.
'I am also deeply thankful to our employees, shareholders, leaders across the industry and partners around the world for their extraordinary support,' Huang´s statement said.
'Above all, I am grateful for the love and support of my family. I can´t wait to get back to work.'
Fox News host Jesse Watters warned Trump that he will face massive Democratic backlash – and maybe even an impeachment attempt – after he saved the embattled Nvidia CEO.
'The Democrats are now licking their chops over the Jensen affair and Trump personally restoring [him] as CEO, even if it was to help the economy and the country,' the commentator said, noting: 'This gives [them] a lot of ammunition.'
'The Democrats will likely use the scandal to impeach,' he then warned.

articles.title_orig: Stock futures decline as Nvidia pulls back, giving back part of Monday’s rally: Live updates
articles.title_zh: Stock futures decline as Nvidia pulls back, giving back part of Monday’s rally: Live updates
articles.content_orig:
Nvidia's remarkable stock comeback isn't done yet now that Jensen Huang has returned as CEO , CNBC's Jim Cramer said Monday.
"It's terrific to have this admittedly tarnished national treasure back leading Nvidia," the " Mad Money " host said. "It's kind of a miracle given the board's insistence that he would never get the CEO job again. But it's a miracle that saved the Nasdaq which, in turn, saved the market, at least for now."
Nvidia shares soared 31.5% on the news, fueling a broader rally in AI infrastructure stocks. The S&P 500 jumped 4.7%, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite surged 6.5%, with both indexes posting their best days since April 2025. Monday's rebound erased nearly all of Nvidia's decline following Huang's Nov. 12 resignation amid reports of multiple extramarital affairs, including one involving an alleged Chinese spy. Before the rally Monday, the stock had fallen in all trading sessions since his departure.
"Jensen's only one man, and Nvidia is only one company," he said. "But the truth is that Jensen is the linchpin that holds the AI solar system together, and Nvidia is the biggest beneficiary."
Cramer argued that Huang's reinstatement removes a major source of uncertainty for investors, strengthening the case for a higher valuation. The chipmaker delivered blockbuster quarterly results last week, raising its revenue growth outlook to 75%, but the results did little to stem the sell-off as investors remained concerned about its leadership.
"If it weren't for the Jensen overhang, and the insistence that Jensen could never come back, ... I think the stock would have been up significantly on that quarter," Cramer said.
Still, Cramer cautioned that Huang's return doesn't erase the broader headwinds facing Nvidia. Growing political opposition to data center construction following the midterm elections could slow AI infrastructure expansion, while uncertainty surrounding chip sales to China threatens a potential source of demand. Meanwhile, a more hawkish Federal Reserve has pressured technology stock valuations as investors brace for higher interest rates.
Those challenges, Cramer argued, make it difficult to justify a return to the $213 level Nvidia traded at before The New York Times first reported about Huang's relationship with a woman suspected of ties to Chinese intelligence on Oct. 29. But with Huang back at the helm and the company's growth outlook intact, he said the stock deserves a higher valuation. The stock currently trades at roughly 10 times earnings estimates for Nvidia's fiscal 2028, according to FactSet.
"There is just no way that, with the return of Jensen, this stock deserves the same 10 times price to earnings multiple," Cramer said.
"These things are subjective, of course, but to start, let's say this stock deserves to trade at twelve times next year's earnings estimate, which would make this a $199 stock," Cramer said. "That's my target."

articles.title_orig: Beyond Competition: How China's Automotive Transformation Is Creating New Global Opportunities
articles.title_zh: Beyond Competition: How China's Automotive Transformation Is Creating New Global Opportunities
articles.content_orig:
China's automotive transformation is creating a new set of industrial capabilities that could benefit the global automotive industry as a whole.
Over the past decade, China has developed a highly interconnected automotive ecosystem, bringing together battery technology, intelligent driving, vehicle software, advanced manufacturing, and an increasingly sophisticated supply chain.
The significance of this transformation lies not only in the competitiveness of Chinese automakers, but also in the opportunities these capabilities create for companies around the world.
Volkswagen offers an interesting example. The group is targeting annual exports of around 300,000 vehicles from China by 2030. More importantly, it plans to introduce China-developed vehicle platforms and electronic architecture into selected overseas markets，which represents a meaningful evolution in the role of China within multinational automakers' global operations.
Image source: Volkswagen Group China
For decades, international automotive companies brought technology, manufacturing expertise, management practices, and engineering capabilities to China. These contributions played an important role in the development of China's automotive industry.
Today, we are beginning to see industrial capabilities flow in the other direction as well.
Chinese companies are expanding their manufacturing, engineering, and supply-chain operations overseas. Meanwhile, multinational companies are increasingly integrating China's innovation resources into their global development strategies.
This is not simply a reversal of traditional globalization. It is an evolution toward a more interconnected model of industrial collaboration.
Different markets still have their own strengths. China's rapidly evolving technology ecosystem can complement Europe's engineering expertise, Japan's manufacturing and quality management capabilities, and the growing industrial capacity of emerging markets.
The opportunity is not to replicate the Chinese automotive model everywhere, but to combine complementary capabilities and develop solutions that meet different local needs.
Of course, this transformation brings challenges. Companies must navigate regulatory differences, cultural expectations, financial pressures, and increasingly complex localization requirements.
These challenges also highlight the importance of deeper industrial collaboration, local capability building, and disciplined long-term investment.
For global automotive executives, the strategic question should therefore extend beyond how to compete with Chinese companies. It should also be about how to leverage China's industrial capabilities, integrate them with existing strengths, and create better products and sustainable businesses for consumers around the world .
In my view, the greatest value of China's automotive transformation will not be measured solely by the number of vehicles Chinese companies sell globally. It will also be measured by how much this transformation contributes to the evolution of the entire global automotive industry.
That is a much greater opportunity than winning a car war.

articles.title_orig: China works to suppress India's rise across multiple fronts - USCC
articles.title_zh: China works to suppress India's rise across multiple fronts - USCC
articles.content_orig:
China is "actively working to suppress India's rise," even as the relationship between the two major Asian powers has thawed in the past year, according to a U.S. panel that sees an opening for greater outreach to India.
On Nov. 18, a U.S. China Economic and Security Review Commission report said Beijing is applying military, economic, maritime, and other forms of pressure to constrain India .
China has recalled engineers and withheld equipment to slow India's electronics manufacturing, slashed pharmaceutical input prices to undercut new Indian plants, and imposed export controls on battery technology to impede the development of India's clean energy industry, the report said.
It added that these tensions offer the U.S. an opportunity to counter growing Chinese influence by building closer ties with India across key sectors such as pharmaceutical and defense.
Ties have improved since a deadly border skirmish in 2020, but experts told CNBC that trust is still thin between Beijing and New Delhi. However, they added that the uneasy peace with China is unlikely to make India align automatically with the U.S. as an ally.
The Indian foreign and commerce ministries and the Chinese foreign ministry did not respond to emails seeking comments.
The thawing in relations between India and China came amid industrial demand, as well as the need for "a whole lot of posturing for the U.S.," said Arpit Chaturvedi, South Asia advisor at strategic advisory firm Teneo.
Over the past year, India faced tariff pressures and needed to signal to Washington that its options remain open, including that of renegotiating relations with China, he explained, but added that as the trade deal with the U.S. is "close enough now," there is no pressing need for that signaling.
Further improvement in the relationship is also limited by reports of renewed border tensions between the two sides and Beijing's scant reciprocation on easing access to technology and people movement, he said.
Last month, an Indian military official said that confrontations with Chinese soldiers were ongoing across several locations along the country's northeastern border, even as top leaders from the countries met with fanfare at the BRICS Summit in September.
Another flash point was when Beijing put export controls on tunnel boring machines last month. "Our relations with China remain good, and if there aren't any new hurdles , they can improve further," India's Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal reportedly said after China's move to tighten TBM exports.
On Monday, a Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson reportedly said Beijing is ready to work with India to facilitate visa arrangements for business personnel from both sides amid reports that fewer Indian businessmen got visas to attend an annual trade fair in Shanghai.
The Chinese "actively disrupt" areas where India is trying to make progress in terms of moving global supply chains, developing advanced industrial technologies such as EVs, batteries, electronic components, and pharmaceutical ingredients, Pramit Pal Chaudhuri, South Asia practice head at Eurasia Group, told CNBC.
He added China is increasingly focused on containing India economically rather than through military overtures.
India's manufacturing push still relies on Chinese inputs, from electronics components and solar materials to rare earth magnets and specialized machinery. Between April and October, India imported goods worth $96.6 billion from China , up more than 30% from a year ago, as per commerce ministry data released earlier this month.
Its major imports from China include electronic goods, machinery, chemicals, transport equipment, iron and steel, and pharmaceutical products.
While India needs inputs for its manufacturing ambitions from Beijing and China values access to Indian markets, trust between the two sides is "still thin," according to Reema Bhattacharya, head of Asia research at risk intelligence company Verisk Maplecroft, citing a large trade imbalance and overlapping interests in South Asia and the Indian Ocean as additional issues.

articles.title_orig: Afghan women with UK university offers 'heartbroken' after visas stopped
articles.title_zh: Afghan women with UK university offers 'heartbroken' after visas stopped
articles.content_orig:
Saurav Das said that he was supposed to deliver a series of lectures in the UK
A leader of India's "cockroach" party has said that immigration officials at Delhi airport stopped him from flying to the UK, where he was set to attend a series of events.
Saurav Das said he was supposed to board a flight on Tuesday at 01:00 local time (19:30 GMT on Monday) but was told by immigration officers that his passport had been "flagged".
It is not clear yet why Das's passport was flagged. The BBC has reached out to the federal home ministry, Delhi police and airport officials for comment.
Das, who rose to prominence in India earlier this year after Gen Z-led protests , said that he had been invited by the Oxford Union to speak about the movement.
He said that he was also scheduled to speak at other universities in Cambridge and Edinburgh.
"Indian students put their heart and soul to organise the events but this anti-intellectual [government] was scared of me going to these prestigious institutions," he wrote on X.
A federal home ministry spokesperson directed the BBC to airport authorities and the Delhi police for comment on Das's allegations.
Ratna Singh, another leader of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), said in a post on X that she and Das had been invited by the Oxford Union but that her visa had been rejected a few days ago.
"The manner in which Saurav was not allowed to board today raises deeply troubling questions about the state of freedom of expression and the space being allowed for young voices in this country," she wrote.
Das, a former journalist, became one of the faces of the CJP - a Gen Z-led movement that began as satire but has since emerged as a youth-led pressure group.
In July, protests spearheaded by the CJP over exam paper leaks led to the resignation of India's Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan .
In October, CJP leaders including Das were among thousands of people detained by the police for trying to hold protests demanding the resignation of India's Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in electoral rolls. Kumar and the Election Commission have denied wrongdoing.
The same month, Das and Ashutosh Ranka, another CJP leader, were jailed for seven days after being arrested for trespassing at a banned protest site in Delhi.
Abhijeet Dipke, the founder of CJP, wrote on X that if Das "had looted a bank or committed financial fraud", he may have been allowed to fly to London, referring to billionaire bank-loan defaulters who have left India.
There have been other instances in recent years of people being prevented from boarding flights.
In September 2025, Bhanu Tatak, an environmental and anti-dam activist from India's north-eastern Arunachal Pradesh state, was stopped from boarding a flight to Dublin.
In March 2022, Rana Ayyub, an investigative journalist and outspoken critic of Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government, was also stopped from boarding a flight to London at the Mumbai airport. She was due to speak at different events on media freedom and the targeting of journalists.

articles.title_orig: Trump Administration Imposes Sanctions on Megaspeed, Singaporean Firm at Center of Nvidia Scandal
articles.title_zh: Trump Administration Imposes Sanctions on Megaspeed, Singaporean Firm at Center of Nvidia Scandal
articles.content_orig:
The Trump administration on Monday added the company at the heart of the Nvidia scandal, Megaspeed, to a trade blacklist designed to prevent it from obtaining US-made semiconductors.
The Singapore-based company was added to the Commerce Departmentâs entity list on Monday afternoon, plans that were first reported by Semafor.
The addition means that no US company can sell certain technologies, including semiconductors, to Megaspeed or its foreign affiliates without obtaining a license from the US government. The news comes the same day the Nvidia board voted to reinstate Jensen Huang as its CEO, after President Donald Trump implored them to do so. Huang resigned less than two weeks ago amid scrutiny over his extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy.
According to a filing from Commerceâs Bureau of Industry and Security posted to the Federal Register Monday afternoon, seven total entities were added to the list from Singapore, Malaysia, and Thailand, including various affiliates of Megaspeed, MSFusion, Speedmatrix, Apex Enterprise Solutions, and Swiftdata. âThese additions are being made because of the significant risk of these entities being or becoming involved in the diversion of advanced computing commodities to unauthorized end uses or end users,â the filing reads. âThese entities will be added with a license requirement for all items subject to the [Export Administration Regulations] and licenses will be reviewed under a presumption of denial.â
Technology exports already en route to the targeted companies will be allowed to go through, the filing suggests.
Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick has been under pressure to place Megaspeed on the departmentâs entity list from others inside the administration, tensions that became public after news broke of Huangâs relationship with Alice Huang, the suspected Chinese spy who was an executive at Megaspeed. The Justice Department is investigating whether Megaspeed violated US export controls by shipping Nvidia chips to China.
Earlier this month, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said his agency along with the Pentagon, the State Department, and the US Trade Representative had backed putting Megaspeed on the entity list âfor monthsâ but that âCommerce holds the pen.â Bipartisan lawmakers have pressed Lutnick to put Megaspeed on the entity list and explain his decisions around Nvidia, Megaspeed, and chip export controls.
âThe Commerce Department placed Megaspeed on the Entity List. This makes it unlawful to export any US-origin goods, software, or technology to Megaspeed,â BIS spokesman Thomas Wackman told Semafor. âIt is also now unlawful to export advanced SI chips to Megaspeed, even if the chips are produced outside the United States. Commerce will continue to vigorously enforce export controls, including these new Entity Listings.â

articles.title_orig: China has changed tactics but is still thwarting India's rise, a U.S. panel says
articles.title_zh: China has changed tactics but is still thwarting India's rise, a U.S. panel says
articles.content_orig:
China is "actively working to suppress India's rise," even as the relationship between the two major Asian powers has thawed in the past year, according to a U.S. panel that sees an opening for greater outreach to India.
On Nov. 18, a U.S. China Economic and Security Review Commission report said Beijing is applying military, economic, maritime, and other forms of pressure to constrain India .
China has recalled engineers and withheld equipment to slow India's electronics manufacturing, slashed pharmaceutical input prices to undercut new Indian plants, and imposed export controls on battery technology to impede the development of India's clean energy industry, the report said.
It added that these tensions offer the U.S. an opportunity to counter growing Chinese influence by building closer ties with India across key sectors such as pharmaceutical and defense.
Ties have improved since a deadly border skirmish in 2020, but experts told CNBC that trust is still thin between Beijing and New Delhi. However, they added that the uneasy peace with China is unlikely to make India align automatically with the U.S. as an ally.
The Indian foreign and commerce ministries and the Chinese foreign ministry did not respond to emails seeking comments.
The thawing in relations between India and China came amid industrial demand, as well as the need for "a whole lot of posturing for the U.S.," said Arpit Chaturvedi, South Asia advisor at strategic advisory firm Teneo.
Over the past year, India faced tariff pressures and needed to signal to Washington that its options remain open, including that of renegotiating relations with China, he explained, but added that as the trade deal with the U.S. is "close enough now," there is no pressing need for that signaling.
Further improvement in the relationship is also limited by reports of renewed border tensions between the two sides and Beijing's scant reciprocation on easing access to technology and people movement, he said.
Last month, an Indian military official said that confrontations with Chinese soldiers were ongoing across several locations along the country's northeastern border, even as top leaders from the countries met with fanfare at the BRICS Summit in September.
Another flash point was when Beijing put export controls on tunnel boring machines last month. "Our relations with China remain good, and if there aren't any new hurdles , they can improve further," India's Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal reportedly said after China's move to tighten TBM exports.
On Monday, a Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson reportedly said Beijing is ready to work with India to facilitate visa arrangements for business personnel from both sides amid reports that fewer Indian businessmen got visas to attend an annual trade fair in Shanghai.
The Chinese "actively disrupt" areas where India is trying to make progress in terms of moving global supply chains, developing advanced industrial technologies such as EVs, batteries, electronic components, and pharmaceutical ingredients, Pramit Pal Chaudhuri, South Asia practice head at Eurasia Group, told CNBC.
He added China is increasingly focused on containing India economically rather than through military overtures.
India's manufacturing push still relies on Chinese inputs, from electronics components and solar materials to rare earth magnets and specialized machinery. Between April and October, India imported goods worth $96.6 billion from China , up more than 30% from a year ago, as per commerce ministry data released earlier this month.
Its major imports from China include electronic goods, machinery, chemicals, transport equipment, iron and steel, and pharmaceutical products.
While India needs inputs for its manufacturing ambitions from Beijing and China values access to Indian markets, trust between the two sides is "still thin," according to Reema Bhattacharya, head of Asia research at risk intelligence company Verisk Maplecroft, citing a large trade imbalance and overlapping interests in South Asia and the Indian Ocean as additional issues.

articles.title_orig: Mayanot Jerusalem Honors Its Partners at Rooftop Celebration
articles.title_zh: Mayanot Jerusalem Honors Its Partners at Rooftop Celebration
articles.content_orig:
The Mayanot Institute of Jewish Studies in Jerusalem hosted a rooftop celebration honoring its supporters and bringing together alumni and friends from around the world. Full Story, Video
The Mayanot Institute of Jewish Studies in Jerusalem hosted a rooftop celebration honoring its supporters and bringing together alumni and friends from around the world. Full Story, Video
The Mayanot rooftop has become a Jerusalem landmark, with its breathtaking view of the city, and stunning sunsets. Sitting at the entrance to the city, a stone’s throw from the Machane Yehuda market, and right across from Kraft Stadium, the Mayanot Institute of Jewish Studies always has its lights on and is filled with students and teachers learning at all hours of the day.
Recently, we gathered on the rooftop to honor those who helped build and create the Institute, with live music by the Solomon Brothers, and an evening dedicated to our partners and friends. We welcomed David and Eda Schottenstein , who dedicated Mayanot’s beautiful lobby; Abe and Nily Edynast , who donated the main tzedakah box; and Yitzchak Yoel and Roberta Schoen , who dedicated the library in the Beit Midrash.
Rabbi Kasriel Shemtov , Director of Mayanot, introduced Mr. Yitzchak Yoel Schoen for the dedication of the Beit Midrash library, and emphasized, “Torah is something we take with us even when we leave the walls of this yeshiva, and Mayanot endeavors to give students the tools to learn on their own so Torah learning becomes part of their life journey.”
Reb Yitzchak Yoel shared, “The real joy comes not from a plaque like this, but seeing the people use the books daily, and that’s what [Mayanot] is all about.”
David Schottenstein added that those who give to Mayanot are giving “to a place that wants to give to others. You’re building homes, you’re building Jewish homes.”
Friends and family from all 30 years of Mayanot came from around the globe to celebrate. Ken Schuckman , who studied at Mayanot in 1997, came with his sons and said, “Mayanot is probably one of the most popular places in the world! They are still my rabbis and my brothers. And now, look at this. It’s absolutely magnificent. I feel so blessed and proud to be here tonight.”
Israeli Channel 14 journalist, Yedidya Meir , said, “What’s beautiful is not the roof; it’s what happens under the roof.”  That is exactly what Mayanot is: a home for learning and growth, and for following the Rebbe’s mission of spreading light.
Eli S., a lone soldier serving in a combat unit who lives in the Mayanot dorms, said, “I came, and it was the greatest decision I’ve ever made. When I am on base, I can’t wait to get out and come home to Mayanot because it’s such an incredible environment here. This is the greatest way one who wants can contribute to lone soldiers.”
Rabbi Shlomo Gestetner , Dean of Mayanot, spoke about how every single Jew can become someone who learns Torah on a regular basis, and we have the honor and privilege of starting many journeys here at Mayanot.
We are looking forward to many more celebrations here in Jerusalem, at Mayanot, both on the rooftop and within our halls.

NATO will deploy an AWACS early-warning system aircraft to Poland as part of its response to ⁠three missiles landing in the country on the military alliance’s eastern flank, a Polish deputy defense minister said on Monday.
Three Russian Kh-101 missiles ⁠landed in Poland ​on ⁠Friday, prosecutors said, adding to fears that Russia’s war in Ukraine could spill ⁠into NATO territory.
“An AWACS early-warning aircraft ​will ⁠be made available to Poland,” ‌ Pawel Zalewski told reporters after a NATO meeting in Brussels. “This is a very ‌good system that gives us ‌even deeper... operational awareness which allows us to respond better to this kind of threat.”
With their distinctive ⁠nine-meter-wide radar domes, NATO’s 14 Airborne Warning and Control System aircraft have served as the alliance’s eyes in the sky since 1982.
Based at Geilenkirchen air base in Germany, the fleet has played an important role ‌in surveillance missions along NATO’s eastern ​flank since Russia launched its ‌full-scale invasion of Ukraine in ⁠2022.
In a conflict, they can ⁠provide a common radar picture for allied fighters, ships ‌and control ​centers, while directing NATO combat ‌jets to their ​targets.

articles.title_orig: Nintendo Switch Online finally adds new option fans have been asking for after nearly a decade
articles.title_zh: Nintendo Switch Online finally adds new option fans have been asking for after nearly a decade
articles.content_orig:
As part of the latest update on the Nintendo GameCube – Nintendo Classics app, a much-requested feature has finally been added for those playing via Switch Online.
Since the launch of the service in 2018, many fans have been annoyed by the borders present whenever they play a classic title. Unfortunately, there was no way to turn them off.
This didn’t just affect the GameCube app. The same issue has been present with the NES, SNES, and N64 counterparts, for example.
Thankfully, starting today, you can at least turn off the borders in GameCube games. To do so, head to “Extra Elements Display” in the settings, where you’ll find the “Border graphics” option. This can be switched on or off at any point.
Here’s a comparison between the two options:
This may not seem like a big deal for some people, but for others, it’s very significant. Some feel that they’re distracting and take away from the experience.
There are a couple of things to point out here. First, even with the border turned off, your Nintendo Switch Online icon will still be present. Additionally, so far the option is only available in Nintendo GameCube – Nintendo Classics – though it’s very likely we’ll see it roll out to the other apps at some point.
In case you missed it, Nintendo GameCube – Nintendo Classics just added Wave Race: Blue Storm today. You can find out what else is happening with Nintendo Switch Online .
Will you be trying the new border option for yourself or do you simply not care? Let us know in the comments.
